verdict: Avoid new sponge iron and ferro alloy exposure in Jharsuguda; the data call is Avoid and the news flow does not lift it.
title: Jharsuguda sponge iron & ferro alloys: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business is
**A Jharsuguda sponge iron or ferro alloy unit buys iron ore and coal, burns them through a kiln or furnace, and sells a commodity priced off steel and alloy benchmarks.** Cash is made on the spread between input cost and realisation, not on brand or customer loyalty. Power is a large cost line, so a unit with waste-heat recovery or captive generation earns a wider spread than one buying grid power. **Capex is heavy and lumpy — a 1,000-TPD sponge iron plant plus a 21-MVA ferro alloy unit and captive power is the typical project shape [9] — so debt is usually term debt against a commodity cash flow.** Working capital sits in coal and ore inventory and in receivables from steel traders; collect the actual inventory days and receivable days from the customer, because the sources do not give them for this city.

## What has changed
**Odisha is running behind the country on both demand signals: GST collections up 0.5% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1%, and electricity demand up 5.1% against India's 9.5% [D].** That is a local demand signal, not a company one, and it says the state's offtake is soft. **Brent at $113/bbl sits above the $75–100 band [D], which raises freight and coal-linked costs across the chain.** India-wide, IIP for NIC 24 (basic metals) grew only 2.4% YoY to Aug-2026 [D], so the end market is not pulling hard.

## Where the growth is
**The peer read is mixed and instructive: Shyam Metalics grew Q4 FY26 revenue 27% YoY on 22% higher volumes [2], but its sponge iron volume fell 2.33% YoY in March 2026 even as realisation rose 1.98% to Rs 25,656/MT [3][4].** The growth is in integrated, value-added players, not in standalone sponge iron. **Ask every proposal which side of that line it sits on.**
**Price the loan for the commodity cycle, not for the best year.**
**If monthly power cost per tonne rises while realisation is flat, ask for the contract and the captive availability.** If group exposure grows faster than net worth, stop fresh limits.
watch: Realisation per tonne vs input cost (monthly)
Spread compression two months running -> reprice or seek additional collateral
Rise with flat realisation -> ask for captive or contract evidence
